reader.requirement: At --std 85, every execution of CLOSE (each form: plain, WITH LOCK, WITH NO REWIND, REEL/UNIT, REEL/UNIT FOR REMOVAL; each file-name of a multi-file CLOSE) updates file-name-1's I-O status to the VII.1.3.5 value: '00' for a successful close, '07' for a NO REWIND / REEL / UNIT / FOR REMOVAL phrase on a non-reel medium, '42' for a file not in the open mode, '30' for a permanent error, with any applicable USE procedure taking the unsuccessful ones.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.CloseWithLockLocksFileConnector (from 2002): at 85 the PHYSICAL file is locked (every later OPEN through any file-name is '38'), from 2002 the connector; the CLOSE's own status comes from Close() before the switch and is the same at every edition
the same behaviour, read at the later OPEN
CLOSE WITH LOCK refused only at 2023 (removed); accepted at 85

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|IsActive|DialectLevel in FileRegistry.cs, FileConnector.cs, CloseTable14.cs, SequentialIoEmitter.cs and VersionConformancePass.cs CLOSE visitors; CloseCell (Table 14 lookup and the '07'/'42' arms) and FileConnector.Close carry no edition test, and the 1985 Table 1 non-reel column (C / C,E / C,H / F / F) gives the same cells.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: not the status update itself; at 85 CLOSE WITH LOCK locks the physical file (a second SELECT of it then OPENs '38', at 2014 '00'), and CLOSE WITH LOCK is legal at 85 but removed at 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses cover the close forms and the '42' status; not exercised here: multi-file CLOSE per-file status, the absent-OPTIONAL close, CLOSE after a failed OPEN, relative/indexed files listed in the CLOSE, the 85 physical-file lock

probes.printed: NEVER-OPENED 42 (USE ran) / PLAIN 00 / TWICE 42 (USE ran) / REEL 07 / UNIT REMOVAL 07 / NO REWIND 07 / LOCK 00 / OPEN AFTER LOCK 38 / CLOSE AFTER FAILED OPEN 42 / OPTIONAL ABSENT 00 / REL NEVER-OPENED 42, REL 00 / IDX NEVER-OPENED 42, IDX 00
probes.expected: VII.1.3.5: 00 success, 07 phrase on non-reel medium (REEL keeps the file open per Table 1 F, so the later CLOSEs still find it open), 42 not open, 38 after LOCK; GR4 updates the status every time

probes.printed: CLOSE SQ SQ2 RL (SQ2 not open): USE FS=00 F2=42 FR=00 / MULTI 00 42 00
probes.expected: GR8: as separate CLOSEs, each file's status updated

probes.printed: error COBOL1693 CLOSE 'RL' with the REEL/UNIT phrase ... only with a sequential-organization file; same for NO REWIND
probes.expected: the relative CLOSE format of 1985 has no REEL/UNIT or NO REWIND

probes.printed: --std 85: LOCK 00 / LOCK AGAIN 42 / OTHER NAME 38; --std 2014: LOCK 00 / LOCK AGAIN 42 / OTHER NAME 00
probes.expected: 85: Table 1 E, 'The file is locked and cannot be opened again during this execution of this run unit'

reader.notes: CLOSE sets the status through one dispatch (CloseCell over Table 14) whose non-reel cells match the 1985 Table 1; every form and the multi-file case printed the VII.1.3.5 value at --std 85. The '30' arm (MappedCloseCore) was read, not provoked: no host failure could be induced from a probe.

refuter.evidence: r4/q1.cob at --std 85: OUTPUT CLOSE REEL 07 then WRITE 00 (file stays open, Table 1 F); CLOSE WITH NO REWIND 07 then CLOSE 42 (H: closed as if no phrase); INPUT CLOSE UNIT 07 then READ continues 00; CLOSE WITH LOCK 00 then again 42; absent OPTIONAL EXTEND 05/close 00. r4/q2.cob: absent OPTIONAL INPUT CLOSE REEL 00 (file stays open), NO REWIND 00, LOCK 00 then OPEN 38; I-O CLOSE REEL FOR REMOVAL 07, REWRITE then 43, CLOSE 00. The absent-OPTIONAL REEL giving 00 rather than 07 is a reading: GR5 says no reel/unit processing, and VII.1.3.5 lets the implementor pick when more than one value applies. cite.py: 'OK §1985:VII.4.2.4 GR3', 'OK §1985:VII.4.2.4 GR5', 'OK §1985:VII.1.3.5 GRL2.1'.
